$note: A clause register that an interpreter evaluates. Assembled by _phase0/build-register.mjs from the domain's published registers plus evaluation.json. Do not edit by hand.

source.$schema_note: Clause register for the MAS/IMDA Guidelines on Shared Responsibility Framework (issued 24 October 2024, effective 16 December 2024) and the paragraphs of the E-Payments User Protection Guidelines (amended 24 October 2024, effective 16 December 2024) that the SRF incorporates. Every clause carries a source pin (document, paragraph, page of the retrieved PDF), a duty holder, a tier of the loss waterfall, a disposition and its basis. `duty_holder` and `tier` are fields of THIS register; _phase0/build-register.mjs does not copy them into register.json (FINDINGS.md F-03). Ambiguities are registered in ambiguities.json and never resolved here.
source.decomposition_note: ENCODED: SRF sections 1 (application and the card exclusion), 2 (the two scope definitions as evaluable limbs; the rest as DEFINITIONAL), 3 (two account-user duties), 4.1 to 4.4, 5.1 to 5.2.3, 6.1 to 6.9, 7.1 to 7.14 and footnotes 1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 14, 15, 16. EUPG: only the paragraphs the SRF names or depends on (1.5, 2.1 four terms, 3.1, 3.14, 3.17, 3.18, 3.20, 4.11, 4.14, 4.20, 4.21, 5.2, 5.5, 8.1). NOT ENCODED: SRF 1.2 and 1.3 (descriptive, no requirement); the whole of EUPG sections 4 (other than the paragraphs above), 6 (erroneous transactions), 7 (disputed investigations) and 8.2 to 8.6, deferred by ruling of the session brief (register over ~150 clauses trims EUPG detail; FINDINGS.md F-02). Where the SRF says a duty is `[From paragraph N of the EUPG]` the SRF clause carries both pins and the EUPG paragraph is not a second clause: the SRF text restates the operative content and Section 6 assesses the SRF wording.

dispositions.$declared_in_source_register: MECHANICAL, JUDGMENT, CONDITIONAL, DERIVED, DEFINITIONAL, INSTRUCTION, as _interpreter/register.schema.json declares them. No EVIDENTIAL clause: the SRF frames no burden of proof. No ILLUSTRATIVE clause.

entries.question: The SRF's limb (a) says `all of whom are individuals`; the EUPG's says `either individuals or sole proprietors`. Is a sole proprietor's account a protected account for an SRF claim?

competing_readings.reading: SRF wording governs an SRF claim: individuals only
competing_readings.basis: The SRF defines `protected account` itself at 2.1 rather than importing the EUPG's definition, and 2.2 defers to the Acts only for expressions the SRF does not define.

competing_readings.reading: EUPG wording governs: sole proprietors included
competing_readings.basis: SRF 1.1(a) applies the Guidelines to issuers of `a protected account` and 4.1 draws the FI duties from the EUPG, whose protected account admits sole proprietors; the EUPG was amended on the same day, and the narrower SRF limb may be an omission.

entries.textual_basis: SRF 2.1 `protected account` (a), p.3: `all of whom are individuals`. EUPG 2.1 `protected account` (a), p.5: `all of whom are either individuals or sole proprietors` [Amended on 24 October 2024].
entries.materiality: Decisive for every sole-proprietor claim: in or out of scope.

entries.question: `on a real-time basis` (4.2.2, 4.2.3) is not defined. How late can an alert be and still be real-time?

competing_readings.reading: Sent at the moment of the event, by an automated path
competing_readings.basis: EUPG 4.10(b): `sent on a real time basis for each transaction`, which reads as per-event automation rather than a latency figure.

competing_readings.reading: Sent within a period short enough for the holder to act before the loss
competing_readings.basis: The duties exist so the holder can report and block (4.2.4); an alert that arrives after the funds have left serves nothing.

entries.materiality: Decides whether a delayed alert is a breach. The register takes the FI's recorded assessment of real-timeness as the fact; it cannot measure latency against an undefined limit.

entries.question: 6.4(a) requires that the FI `has complied with all of its duties set out in paragraph 4.2`. Where a duty never arose (no token was activated; the account was not rapidly drained; the holder declined notifications), has the FI complied with it?

competing_readings.reading: counts_as_complied
competing_readings.basis: A conditional duty whose condition did not occur cannot have been breached, and `complied with all` is satisfied by the absence of any breach. This is the reading under which 6.7 is reachable in the ordinary case.

competing_readings.reading: not_a_compliance_finding
competing_readings.basis: `has complied` is an affirmative finding about conduct; a duty that never arose produced no conduct to find compliant, and the session brief requires the consumer outcome to rest on affirmative per-duty findings on both tiers. Under this reading a claim with any never-arisen duty cannot reach 6.7.

entries.textual_basis: SRF 6.4(a), p.9; 6.7, p.10: `Where the responsible FI is not expected to bear the loss under paragraph 6.2`.
entries.materiality: Decisive for the Telco tier and for 6.7 in nearly every claim, since at least one of the five duties has a precondition. WIRED AS A GUARD: unresolved, srf/6.4/a/fi-complied-all is undetermined wherever a duty is not_applicable, and the waterfall stops at the FI tier.

entries.question: 6.2 puts the loss on the FI `if the loss arises from any non-compliance`, while 6.4(a) asks only whether the FI `has complied with all of its duties`. Where a 4.2 duty was breached but the loss did not arise from it, who bears?

competing_readings.reading: Causation required: the FI does not bear under 6.2, the Telco does not bear under 6.4 (6.4(a) fails), and 6.7 puts the loss on the account holder
competing_readings.basis: The words of 6.2 and 6.4 read together. The register encodes this.

competing_readings.reading: Any breach suffices: `arises from` is satisfied by the breach's existence
competing_readings.basis: The consultation response and the infographic speak of the FI bearing the loss `if FI breaches SRF duties`, without a causal step; and the alternative leaves the consumer bearing a loss after an FI breach, which the framework's stated purpose cannot intend.

entries.textual_basis: SRF 6.2, p.9; 6.4(a), p.9; 6.7, p.10; infographic (Outcome Stage): `If FI breaches SRF duties`.
entries.materiality: Decisive whenever a breach is found and causation is denied: row (true, denied) of srf/6.2/fi-bears yields fi_not_liable_under_6.2 and, through 6.4(a), account_holder_bears.

entries.question: 5.2.3 requires the Telco to `implement an anti-scam filter ... to determine if it contains any URL that matches that of a known malicious URL in a designated database`. Is the duty breached when a filter exists but the phishing SMS, whose URL was in the database, was delivered?

competing_readings.reading: filter_in_place: the duty is to implement the filter; a delivery despite it is a performance question, not a breach
competing_readings.basis: The verb is `implement`; the sentence describes what the filter determines, not a guarantee of blocking.

competing_readings.reading: specific_sms_blocked: the duty is to block SMS containing listed URLs; a listed URL delivered is a breach
competing_readings.basis: The heading of 5.2.3 is `implements an anti-scam filter over SMS to block SMS containing malicious URLs`, and a filter that does not block listed URLs is not the filter described.

entries.materiality: Decisive for the Telco tier in every SMS case where the URL was listed. WIRED AS A GUARD: unresolved, srf/5.2.3/duty is undetermined. Resolution key A5_filter_duty_reading.

entries.question: Once an institution supplies which database is `designated`, is the SMS's URL tested against the database's contents at the instant of delivery or at the time of assessment?

competing_readings.reading: At delivery
competing_readings.basis: The duty is to block SMS as they pass through the network; the database's later contents could not have been consulted.

competing_readings.reading: At assessment
competing_readings.basis: The investigation (7.7.1) is the point at which the Telco `has fulfilled` the duty is judged, and the database is what it is then.

entries.textual_basis: SRF 5.2.3, p.8; footnote 10: `new malicious URLs can emerge rapidly`.
entries.materiality: Decides srf/5.2.3/this-sms-blocked's precondition. The register's fact `sms.url_listed_at_delivery` takes the first reading in its name.

entries.question: Footnote 9 grounds `authorised aggregators` to the SGNIC list. Is membership tested against the list as it stood when the SMS was delivered, or as it stands when the claim is assessed?

competing_readings.reading: As at delivery
competing_readings.basis: The Telco's connection decision was made then.

competing_readings.reading: As at assessment
competing_readings.basis: The list is published without history; the assessor can only read it now.

entries.textual_basis: SRF footnote 9, p.8: `The list of authorised aggregators can be found on SGNIC's website`.
entries.materiality: Decides srf/5.2.1 where an aggregator was added or removed between delivery and assessment. The register takes the list as a supplied fact and does not date it.

entries.question: 7.3 says the holder `should report ... no later than 30 calendar days`. What is the consequence of a later report for the Section 6 outcome?

competing_readings.reading: None stated: the claim proceeds and Section 6 allocates loss on the duties alone
competing_readings.basis: Section 6 names no timeliness condition; footnote 14 contemplates a late report with reasons.

competing_readings.reading: A late claim is outside the workflow and the FI treats it under 7.6
competing_readings.basis: `must furnish ... within 3 calendar days ... in order to facilitate the claims investigation process` reads as a condition of the process.

entries.materiality: Decides whether a late claimant can reach 6.7 at all. The register evaluates the first reading: the waterfall reads no 7.3 result.

entries.question: SRF 7.3 counts 30 days `from when the responsible FI sends the notification alerts`; EUPG 3.14 counts `after receipt of any notification alert`. Which clock?

competing_readings.reading: Sending (SRF)
competing_readings.basis: The SRF is the later and more specific instrument for a seemingly authorised transaction.

competing_readings.reading: Receipt (EUPG)
competing_readings.basis: SRF 3.1 applies EUPG Section 3 `accordingly`, and receipt is what the holder can act on.

entries.materiality: Days between sending and receipt. Two clauses, two clocks: srf/7.3/report-within-30-days and eupg/3.14/report-within-30-days-of-receipt.

entries.question: Where the subscriber who received the SMS is not the account holder and is on a different operator from the holder, which operator is the `responsible Telco`?

competing_readings.reading: The subscriber's operator
competing_readings.basis: 6.6 speaks of `the responsible Telco's subscriber` and the duties in 5.2 are about SMS delivered to subscribers.

competing_readings.reading: The account holder's operator
competing_readings.basis: 7.4 asks for `the name of the responsible Telco whose services the account holder had subscribed to`.

entries.materiality: Decides which Telco investigates and may bear. The register records one Telco's facts and does not name which operator they belong to.

entries.question: Footnote 8(b): `more than 50% of such account balance is transferred out within the last 24 hours`. The last 24 hours before what instant?

competing_readings.reading: Before the transaction that would cross the 50% threshold
competing_readings.basis: 4.2.5(a) speaks of `the online banking payment transaction that would result in the crossing of the threshold`.

competing_readings.reading: A rolling window ending at each transaction to the scammer
competing_readings.basis: `rapidly drained` describes a pattern, and each transaction re-tests it.

entries.materiality: Decides when the block-or-hold duty triggers. The register takes the FI's recorded assessment.

entries.question: 4.2.5(a): block `until it is able to obtain further verification from the account holder`. Is a block released on any contact with the holder, or on a verification that the transactions are intended?

competing_readings.reading: Any further verification step
competing_readings.basis: The words.

competing_readings.reading: Verification that the holder intends the payments
competing_readings.basis: The duty is `directed at detecting seemingly authorised transactions`; a verification that does not test intent detects nothing.

entries.materiality: Decides whether a block released on a scripted call-back satisfies (a). The register records the FI's response as a named alternative and does not test what the verification was.

entries.question: Where activation is non-straight-through, does the 12 hours run from the start of the process (e.g. the mailing) or from the holder's first step?

competing_readings.reading: From the start of the process
competing_readings.basis: `the duration of the non-straight through process counts towards fulfilling the cooling off period`.

competing_readings.reading: From the holder's request
competing_readings.basis: A period the FI controls the start of is not a cooling-off period for the holder.

entries.materiality: Hours. The register does not measure the period (F-05).

entries.question: The SRF's `high-risk activities` list is closed (`means`); the EUPG's is open (`include, but are not limited to`). For 4.2.1 and 4.2.2, is an activity outside the four a high-risk activity?

competing_readings.reading: Closed: the four only
competing_readings.basis: The SRF's own definition and the duties assessed are the SRF's.

competing_readings.reading: Open: the SRF duties are `drawn from` the EUPG (4.1), whose list is open
competing_readings.basis: 4.2.1 and 4.2.2 are `[From paragraph 4.7/4.9 of the EUPG]`.

entries.materiality: Decides whether, e.g., a change of login method triggers the alert duty. The register's fact `fi.events.high_risk_activity` is recorded against the SRF's closed list.

entries.question: `legitimate business or government entity` includes `entities incorporated outside Singapore that offer services to Singapore residents`. Who decides that a foreign entity offers such services, and what of an impersonated individual (a relative, a bank officer by name)?

competing_readings.reading: Entity class only: an impersonated individual is outside limb (a) whatever their role
competing_readings.basis: The definition lists agencies and entities.

competing_readings.reading: Impersonating an officer of an entity is impersonating the entity
competing_readings.basis: Limb (a)'s examples (`FIs, non-banks and government agencies`) are impersonated through people.

entries.textual_basis: SRF 2.1 `legitimate business or government entity`, p.3; `seemingly authorised transaction` (a), p.4.
entries.materiality: Decisive for scope in officer-impersonation cases. The register's enumeration classifies the recorded impersonated entity; the classifier is whoever records the fact.

entries.question: Footnote 8 excludes recurring instructions, GIRO, bill payments, debit card transactions and intrabank transfers `for the avoidance of doubt`. Are the excluded flows removed from the 50% numerator only, or from the opening balance too?

competing_readings.reading: Numerator only
competing_readings.basis: The exclusion is of what `is transferred out`.

competing_readings.reading: Both, so the balance is the balance available to the scammer
competing_readings.basis: `rapidly drained ... to a scammer` is a statement about the scammer's take.

entries.materiality: Can move an account across the 50% line. Not measured (F-05).

entries.question: `any requirement imposed by the Authority on the responsible FI in respect of its provision of any financial service` is an open class. Does it include the EUPG's own `should` expectations, or only Notices and Directions?

competing_readings.reading: Binding requirements only
competing_readings.basis: `imposed` and `requirement`; Guidelines are expectations (SRF 1.4, EUPG 1.4).

competing_readings.reading: Includes Guidelines
competing_readings.basis: EUPG 5.5(c) separately names Section 4 duties, which would be redundant under the first reading only if Guidelines were already in (b).

entries.materiality: Decides how wide 6.3 reaches. Taken as a held judgment.

entries.question: 4.3 applies 4.2 during scheduled downtime `where relevant` and requires alternatives `where applicable`. When is a downtime failure of an alert a breach of 4.2.2 or 4.2.3?

competing_readings.reading: Always: 4.2 applies during downtime
competing_readings.basis: `paragraph 4.2 of these Guidelines applies during a scheduled system downtime`.

competing_readings.reading: Only where an alternative was applicable and not provided
competing_readings.basis: `where relevant` and `where applicable` qualify both sentences.

entries.materiality: Decides breach in a downtime case. The register records no downtime fact and evaluates 4.2 the same way regardless.

entries.question: A responsible Telco is an MNO that deploys, owns or controls infrastructure. An MVNO subscriber's SMS passes through an MNO's network. In an MVNO case, is the host MNO the responsible Telco, or is there none?

competing_readings.reading: The host MNO
competing_readings.basis: The 5.2 duties are about SMS passing through `the responsible Telcos' network`, which is the MNO's.

competing_readings.reading: None: the subscriber's operator is not an MNO and 5.2 binds an operator in respect of its subscribers
competing_readings.basis: 2.1 `subscriber ... in relation to a responsible Telco` means a subscriber of that Telco's services.

entries.materiality: Decides whether the Telco tier arises at all in an MVNO case. The register records `telco.operator_type` and srf/1.1/b answers not_member for `mvno`; the Telco-tier clauses read 7.7 (SMS or not), not 1.1(b), so an MVNO case still evaluates the Telco's duties against whatever Telco's facts are supplied (recorded as a limit, not a reading).

entries.question: Section 6 allocates loss on FI and Telco duties only; Section 3 duties of the account user and EUPG 5.2 recklessness appear nowhere in 6.2 to 6.7. Does an account user's own breach affect the SRF outcome?

competing_readings.reading: No: the SRF waterfall has no consumer-duty tier; the consumer bears only residually
competing_readings.basis: 6.7's condition is the two prior tiers' non-liability and nothing else; the consultation response describes the consumer tier as residual.

competing_readings.reading: Yes, through 6.3 and EUPG 5.4: an FI is not liable under EUPG 5.4 where the loss `does not arise from any failure by any account user to comply with any duty in Section 3`
competing_readings.basis: 6.3 incorporates 5.5(a) and (b), which 5.4 frames; a Section 3 failure could defeat 6.3 though not 6.2.

entries.materiality: Decides whether srf/3.1/*, eupg/3.17 and eupg/5.2 should feed the waterfall. The register emits them and reads none of them in Section 6.

entries.question: 4.2.3 is owed to an account holder `that the responsible FI has been instructed to send transaction notification alerts to`. Where the holder never instructed, or instructed a narrower preference (EUPG 4.11), the duty never arises. Is the FI then to be found `complied` for 6.4(a)?

competing_readings.reading: Yes: the duty is defined by the instruction
competing_readings.basis: Footnote 6 and EUPG 3.1 and 4.11.

competing_readings.reading: No: 4.2.3 as headed (`provides outgoing transaction notification alerts on a real-time basis`) is a capability duty the FI either has or lacks
competing_readings.basis: The heading and the infographic speak of the duty without the instruction condition.

entries.textual_basis: SRF 4.2.3 and footnote 6, p.6; EUPG 3.1, p.8; 4.11, p.18.
entries.materiality: A3's question, arising for this duty in particular. Follows A3's resolution.

entries.question: Each SRF 4.2 duty is `[From paragraph N of the EUPG]` and then restated more narrowly (4.2.3 omits EUPG 4.10(a)-(d)'s content criteria; 4.2.4 omits 4.14's channels and 4.20's characteristics; 4.2.5 narrows 4.21 to a threshold trigger). Is the SRF duty assessed on the SRF's restatement or on the EUPG paragraph it is drawn from?

competing_readings.reading: The SRF restatement
competing_readings.basis: 4.2 says `The following duties from the EUPG are assessed under Section 6` and then states each; the statement is what is assessed.

competing_readings.reading: The EUPG paragraph in full
competing_readings.basis: `[From paragraph N]` is a citation, and 4.1 expects adherence to all of EUPG Section 4.

entries.materiality: Decides whether a notification lacking EUPG 4.10(d)'s content, or a kill switch not on an ATM, is a 4.2 breach. The register evaluates the restatement and emits the EUPG detail as separate `process` records (eupg/4.14, eupg/4.20, eupg/4.21) that the waterfall does not read.

entries.question: `a reporting channel that is available at all times`: is the test whether the channel is generally available, or whether it was available when this account holder tried to use it?

competing_readings.reading: General availability
competing_readings.basis: `provide ... a reporting channel that is available at all times` describes the channel.

competing_readings.reading: Availability at the material time
competing_readings.basis: The duty exists for `prompt reporting and blocking of further seemingly authorised transactions`, which is a moment.

entries.materiality: Decides breach in an outage case. The register's fact is the FI's recorded flag without a time.

entries.question: 4.2.5 `will take effect 6 months from the date these Guidelines are effective`. For a scam spanning the commencement date, which instant is ordered against 16 June 2025: the first transaction, the threshold-crossing one, or the report?

competing_readings.reading: Each transaction separately
competing_readings.basis: The duty is triggered per transaction (4.2.5(a): `the online banking payment transaction that would result in the crossing`).

competing_readings.reading: The claim as a whole, by its first transaction
competing_readings.basis: Section 6 allocates one loss per claim.

entries.textual_basis: SRF 4.4, p.7; media release 24 October 2024, para 3: `a 6-month transition period`.
entries.materiality: Only for claims spanning 16 June 2025. The register orders one instant, `transaction.executed_at`, and the same instant for EUPG 1.5.

entries.question: SRF footnote 12 quotes EUPG 5.5(a) and (b) and omits (c) (non-compliance with any Section 4 duty). Was the omission deliberate, so that an EUPG Section 4 breach outside SRF 4.2 does not shift loss under the SRF?

competing_readings.reading: Deliberate: 6.2 already covers the 4.2 duties and (c) would sweep in the rest of Section 4, which 4.2 deliberately excludes
competing_readings.basis: The structure of 4.2 (`The following duties ... are assessed`).

competing_readings.reading: An oversight, and (c) applies through 4.1's expectation of adherence to all of Section 4
competing_readings.basis: 6.3 is `notwithstanding 6.2` and exists to widen it.

entries.textual_basis: SRF 6.3 and footnote 12, p.9; EUPG 5.5, p.26.
entries.materiality: Decides whether, e.g., a missing EUPG 4.16 warning shifts loss. The register encodes the footnote as written: (a) and (b) only.

entries.question: 5.2.1 (deliver only from authorised aggregators) and 5.2.2 (block those not from authorised aggregators) are one rule stated twice. For `any duty set out in paragraph 5.2` (6.4(b)), does one unauthorised delivery breach one duty or two?

competing_readings.reading: One rule, two statements; breached together
competing_readings.basis: There is no delivery of an unauthorised Sender ID SMS that breaches one and not the other.

competing_readings.reading: Two duties: 5.2.1 is about connections, 5.2.2 about blocking
competing_readings.basis: The 2023 consultation annex lists them separately with different verbs (`Connect only to`, `Block`).

entries.textual_basis: SRF 5.2.1, 5.2.2, p.8; Annex A to the 25 October 2023 media release (superseded; SOURCES.md).
entries.materiality: None for the outcome (a disjunction is the same either way); matters for what the record says was breached. The register emits both.

entries.question: 7.4 says the records `should sufficiently demonstrate` limbs matching 2.1(a)-(c). Is a claim whose records do not demonstrate them outside scope (not a relevant claim), or in scope but unproven?

competing_readings.reading: Evidential only: scope is 2.1's four limbs; 7.4 is what the holder supplies
competing_readings.basis: 7.1.1 assesses scope; 7.4 sits in the Claim Stage as an information request (`may request`).

competing_readings.reading: Constitutive: a claim not demonstrated is not a relevant claim
competing_readings.basis: `in order to facilitate the claims investigation process` (7.3).

entries.materiality: Decides whether a poorly documented claim reaches Section 6. The register keeps 7.4 out of scope (srf/7.1.1 does not read it).

entries.question: Footnote 13: the Telco's involvement `shall be based on any mutually agreed arrangement between the responsible FI and responsible Telco`. Where there is no arrangement, does the FI's duty to inform the Telco (7.7) arise?

competing_readings.reading: Yes: 7.7 is unconditional; the footnote governs 7.1.3 (the Outcome Stage) only
competing_readings.basis: Footnote 13 is attached to `paragraph 7.1.3`.

competing_readings.reading: No arrangement, no referral
competing_readings.basis: The Telco cannot `commence its investigation` without a channel to receive it.

entries.materiality: Decides srf/7.7/inform-telco where no arrangement exists. The register does not record the arrangement.

entries.question: `21 business days` and `45 business days`: are Singapore public holidays business days?

competing_readings.reading: Weekdays excluding public holidays
competing_readings.basis: Ordinary Singapore usage; the Interpretation Act's `business day` excludes public holidays for some purposes.

competing_readings.reading: Weekdays
competing_readings.basis: Neither instrument defines the term.

entries.materiality: Up to a few days per period. The register's business_days unit counts weekdays only, and this is a stated limit of the primitive, not a reading of the text.

entries.question: 6.4(a) requires the FI to have `complied with all of its duties`. Where the FI tier closed `fi_not_liable` because a breach caused no loss (A4, causation denied), 6.4(a) is nonetheless unmet. Does the Telco escape because of an FI breach that shifted no loss?

competing_readings.reading: Yes, on the words: 6.4(a) is about compliance, not liability
competing_readings.basis: 6.4(a) and 6.7 use different predicates (`complied with all`, `not expected to bear`).

competing_readings.reading: No: 6.4(a) should be read as `is not expected to bear under 6.2`, so the tiers chain
competing_readings.basis: Otherwise a non-causal FI breach leaves the consumer bearing a Telco-caused loss.

entries.materiality: Reachable only through A4's causation-denied row. The register encodes the words: srf/6.4/telco-bears reads srf/6.4/a/fi-complied-all, not srf/6/fi-tier.

waiting.$note: The second axis beside lane: what this run of the clause is waiting on. Computed at emission, per run, never stored. See _interpreter/WAITING-AXIS.md.

lanes.$note: Dispositions become data, so the router is a lookup. Named now; NOTHING READS THEM YET. The lookup is total over the dispositions in use, with an explicit no_lane state: a lane names what produces a determination, and a clause that refuses one or supplies a meaning instead has nothing to route.

DEFINITIONAL.no_lane: supplies a meaning; produces no determination to route

INSTRUCTION.no_lane: refuses; produces no determination to route

ungrounded_terms.$note: Two terms the instruments decide outcomes with and supply no meaning for. The interpreter NEVER supplies one. Declared once for the domain.

parts.value: ` is ungrounded: neither the SRF Guidelines nor the EUPG defines it or points to what does

rests_on.value: a meaning supplied by the institution, not by the Guidelines

clauses.source_locator: SRF 1.1(a), p.1; definition of `responsible FI` at 2.1, p.4
clauses.text: banks and relevant payment service providers that have issued a protected account ("responsible financial institutions" or "responsible FIs")
clauses.assertion: The Guidelines apply to the issuer of the protected account only if it is a bank or a relevant payment service provider (a major payment institution licensed for account issuance).
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of the issuer in a closed two-member class recorded as a fact. A finance company or a non-bank card issuer is a responsible FI under the EUPG (2.1) but not under the SRF; the difference is decided by this clause.

clauses.source_locator: SRF 1.1(b), p.1; definition of `responsible Telco` at 2.1, p.4
clauses.text: mobile network operators under the Telecommunications Act 1999 which provide cellular mobile telephone services
clauses.assertion: A responsible Telco is a Mobile Network Operator that deploys, owns or controls cellular network infrastructure and holds spectrum rights. Nothing else is one.
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of the subscriber's operator in a one-member class. An MVNO subscriber has no responsible Telco under this definition (ambiguity A18).

note.value: not_member for an MVNO subscriber (A18). Recorded beside the Telco tier; the tier gates on 7.7, not on this.

clauses.source_locator: SRF footnote 1, p.2; EUPG footnote 3, p.1
clauses.text: the responsibility sharing set out in these Guidelines do not apply to transactions on credit cards, charge cards and debit cards issued in Singapore
clauses.assertion: A claim about a transaction on a Singapore-issued credit, charge or debit card is outside the SRF's responsibility sharing whatever else is true of it.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded boolean about the transaction. Absent is not `not a card transaction`: the clause is undetermined until the fact is recorded.

clauses.text: They should be read in conjunction with the provisions of the relevant legislation ... written directions, notices, codes and other guidelines that MAS or IMDA (as the case may be) may issue
clauses.assertion: The Guidelines neither replace nor override legislation and are not comprehensive.
clauses.disposition_basis: Directs how to read the instrument. No fact of a claim makes it true or false.

clauses.source_locator: SRF 2.1 `protected account` limb (a), p.3, and footnote 2
clauses.text: is held in the name of one or more persons, all of whom are individuals
clauses.assertion: Every holder of the account is an individual. A corporate, partnership or sole-proprietorship account is not a protected account under the SRF.
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of the recorded holder type in a one-member enumeration. The EUPG's limb (a) admits sole proprietors; the SRF's does not (ambiguity A1). The register evaluates the SRF's wording and registers the divergence.

note.value: The SRF's limb: individuals only. A sole proprietor is not_member here and a member under the EUPG (A1).

clauses.text: is capable of having a balance of more than S$1,000 (or equivalent amount expressed in any other currency) at any one time, or is a credit facility
clauses.assertion: Either the account can hold more than S$1,000 or it is a credit facility.
clauses.disposition_basis: A disjunction of two recorded booleans. The S$1,000 capability is recorded as a boolean because the register has no ordered comparison over amounts (F-05); the fact records the FI's own capability flag, not a balance.

clauses.text: is capable of being used for electronic payment transactions
clauses.assertion: The account can be used for electronic payment transactions.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded boolean.

clauses.text: where issued by a relevant payment service provider is a payment account that stores specified e-money
clauses.assertion: If the issuer is a relevant payment service provider, the account must store specified e-money. For a bank-issued account the limb does not arise.
clauses.disposition_basis: An obligation on the account's shape that arises only for one issuer type. `not_applicable` for a bank-issued account is not a pass of limb (d); it is limb (d) never arising.

note.value: not_applicable means the issuer is not a relevant payment service provider, where limb (d) never arises.

clauses.text: "protected account" means any payment account that— (a) ... (b) ... (c) ... and (d) ...
clauses.assertion: All four limbs must hold for the account to be a protected account.
clauses.disposition_basis: Composes the four limb results. Reads no fact of its own. Limb (d)'s `not_applicable` composes as holding because the limb is conditional by its own words (`where issued by a relevant payment service provider`).

note.value: One failing limb decides not_satisfied; satisfied needs all four affirmative (limb (d) may be not_applicable by its own words).

clauses.source_locator: SRF 2.1 `seemingly authorised transaction` limb (a), p.4; `legitimate business or government entity`, p.3
clauses.text: perpetrated through the impersonation of a legitimate business or government entity, e.g., FIs, non-banks and government agencies ("impersonated entity")
clauses.assertion: The scammer impersonated a Singapore Government agency, an entity incorporated in Singapore, or a foreign entity that offers services to Singapore residents. Impersonation of an individual is outside limb (a).
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of the recorded impersonated-entity class in the three-member enumeration the definition gives. Whether a foreign entity `offers services to Singapore residents` is a classification made when the fact is recorded, not here (ambiguity A14).

clauses.source_locator: SRF 2.1 `seemingly authorised transaction` limb (b), p.4, and footnote 3
clauses.text: the scammer, pretending to be the impersonated entity, uses a digital messaging platform (e.g., SMS, email, WhatsApp, social media platforms) to obtain the account user's account credentials
clauses.assertion: The contact that obtained the credentials was over a digital messaging platform. A phone call or a letter is not one.
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of the recorded contact platform in the digital-messaging class. The list in the text is illustrative (`e.g.`); the register's enumeration adds `other_digital` so an unlisted digital platform is a member rather than a gap.

clauses.source_locator: SRF 2.1 `seemingly authorised transaction` limb (c), p.4; `fabricated digital platform`, p.2
clauses.text: the account user enters his account credentials on a fabricated digital platform (e.g., website, application) ("fraudulently obtained credentials")
clauses.assertion: The credentials were entered by the account user on a platform resembling one operated by the FI or the impersonated entity.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded boolean. A credential given over the phone, or a device compromised by malware, does not satisfy limb (c) and the claim is outside the SRF.

clauses.source_locator: SRF 2.1 `seemingly authorised transaction` limb (d), p.4; EUPG footnote 4(a), p.6
clauses.text: the fraudulently obtained credentials are used to perform transactions that the account user did not intend to be performed
clauses.assertion: The account user did not intend the transactions. A payment the user knew of and meant to make, however induced (EUPG footnote 4(a): investment, job, love scams), is not one.
clauses.disposition_basis: Intention is assessed, not read off a record. Taken as an input; never inferred from the other limbs.

note.value: affirmed means the account user did not intend the transactions. not_assessed is a person's absence, not a finding.

clauses.text: any payment transaction which fulfils limbs (a) to (d)
clauses.assertion: All four limbs must hold.
clauses.disposition_basis: Composes the four limbs. Reads no fact of its own.

clauses.text: It will assess if the claim falls within the SRF's scope ("relevant claim")
clauses.assertion: A claim is a relevant claim when the issuer is a responsible FI, the transaction is not a card transaction, the account is a protected account and the transaction is a seemingly authorised transaction.
clauses.disposition_basis: Composes the scope clauses. The responsible-Telco question is not part of scope: a claim with no responsible Telco is still a relevant claim, and the Telco tier answers `not_applicable` (6.4 is confined to scams perpetrated through SMS).

note.value: One affirmative scope failure is not_relevant whatever the others; relevant_claim needs all four affirmative.

clauses.source_locator: SRF 2.1 `high-risk activities`, p.2-3; EUPG 2.1 `high-risk activities`, p.4
clauses.text: "high-risk activities" means— (a) adding of payees ... (b) increasing the transaction limits ... (c) disabling transaction notifications ... and (d) changes in the account holder's contact information
clauses.assertion: The SRF's list is closed (`means`); the EUPG's is open (`include, but are not limited to`). The SRF's closed list is what 4.2.1 and 4.2.2 are assessed against.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies a meaning to 4.2.1 and 4.2.2. Tests nothing.
clauses.operative_weight: An activity outside the four is not a high-risk activity for the cooling-off and alert duties under the SRF, though it may be one under the EUPG (ambiguity A13).

clauses.text: "money" includes currency and e-money but does not include digital payment tokens
clauses.assertion: A transfer of digital payment tokens is not a payment transaction and is outside the SRF.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies a meaning to `payment transaction`. The register records no DPT fact; an institution applying it must classify before recording the transaction.
clauses.operative_weight: Excludes digital payment tokens from every clause that says `payment transaction`.

clauses.text: "SMS" means a text message sent using an electronic service to an end-user on a mobile telephone through a telecommunication service, and excludes text messages sent over social media platforms and those that rely on Over-The-Top ("OTT") applications such as WhatsApp, iMessage, and Rich Communication Services ("RCS")
clauses.assertion: A WhatsApp, iMessage or RCS message is not an SMS. A scam over those platforms is inside limb (b) but is not `perpetrated through SMS`, so the Telco tier never arises.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the meaning `perpetrated through SMS` (7.7) rests on.
clauses.operative_weight: Only `sms` in the contact-platform enumeration is an SMS; `whatsapp`, `social_media` and `other_digital` are not.

clauses.text: "Sender ID SMS" means an SMS with an alphanumeric sender identification
clauses.assertion: An SMS from a local or overseas telephone number is not a Sender ID SMS, and 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 do not reach it; 5.2.3 does.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the precondition of 5.2.1 and 5.2.2.
clauses.operative_weight: 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 arise only when the phishing SMS carried an alphanumeric sender ID.

clauses.text: "subscriber", in relation to a responsible Telco, means— (a) a subscriber of telecommunication services provided by the responsible Telco; or (b) any other person who is authorised ... to use the telecommunication services
clauses.assertion: The subscriber may be a person other than the account holder; 6.6 governs that case.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the meaning 6.6 rests on.
clauses.operative_weight: The Telco's duty runs to its subscriber; whether the subscriber is the account holder is a separate fact 6.6 tests.

clauses.text: The expressions used in these Guidelines shall, except where expressly defined in these Guidelines, have the same meanings as in the applicable Acts
clauses.assertion: Undefined expressions take their statutory meaning.
clauses.disposition_basis: Directs where to look for meanings. Tests nothing.

clauses.text: "unauthorised transaction" ... means any payment transaction initiated by any person without the actual or imputed knowledge and implied or express consent of an account user of the protected account. This includes "seemingly authorised transactions" as defined in the Guidelines to the Shared Responsibility Framework.
clauses.assertion: A seemingly authorised transaction is an unauthorised transaction under the EUPG; a payment the user intended, however induced, is neither.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the meaning limb (d) of the SRF definition rests on, and the EUPG's own exclusions (footnote 4).
clauses.operative_weight: Limb (d) carries footnote 4(a): an intended payment is outside the SRF even where every other limb holds.

clauses.source_locator: EUPG 2.1 `access code`, p.3; SRF footnote 3, p.4
clauses.text: "access code" means a password, code or any other arrangement that the account user must keep secret, that may be required to authenticate any payment transaction or account user
clauses.assertion: `account credentials` in the SRF definition includes an access code and the user ID.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the meaning limb (b) rests on.
clauses.operative_weight: A one-time password sent by SMS is an access code; a card security number printed on the card is not.

clauses.text: (a) is held in the name of one or more persons, all of whom are either individuals or sole proprietors
clauses.assertion: The EUPG admits sole proprietors where the SRF admits individuals only.
clauses.disposition_basis: Registered for the divergence (A1). The SRF's limb is what srf/2.1/protected-account/a/individuals evaluates; this clause supplies the competing meaning and evaluates nothing.
clauses.operative_weight: A sole proprietor's claim is inside the EUPG and, on the SRF's words, outside the SRF.

clauses.text: Responsible FIs are expected to adhere to all the duties set out under Section 4 of the EUPG.
clauses.assertion: All EUPG Section 4 duties bind the responsible FI, but only those in 4.2 are assessed under Section 6.
clauses.disposition_basis: Incorporates a section of another instrument without stating a testable fact of the claim. The EUPG paragraphs the SRF assesses are encoded as the 4.2 clauses; the rest of EUPG Section 4 is not encoded (F-02).

clauses.text: the responsible FI must impose a cooling off period of at least 12 hours where high-risk activities cannot be performed, when a digital security token is activated on a device, or when there is a login to a protected account issued by a relevant payment service provider on a new device
clauses.assertion: When a digital security token was activated, or (for a PSP-issued account) a login occurred on a new device, the FI imposed a cooling-off period of at least 12 hours during which high-risk activities could not be performed.
clauses.disposition_basis: An obligation that arises on an event. The 12-hour floor is a mechanical test the register cannot express: elapsed_within has no hours unit and no primitive orders two durations (F-05), so the floor and the prevention of high-risk activities are taken as the FI's recorded assessments. `not_applicable` means no token was activated and no new-device login occurred; whether that counts as compliance for 6.4(a) is ambiguity A3.

note.value: The 12-hour floor and the block on high-risk activities are the FI's recorded assessments (F-05). not_applicable: no token activated and no PSP new-device login.

clauses.source_locator: SRF footnote 5, p.6; EUPG footnote 13, p.16
clauses.text: If the security token is activated via a non-straight through process (e.g. mailing of registration code), the duration of the non-straight through process counts towards fulfilling the cooling off period.
clauses.assertion: Time spent in a non-straight-through activation process counts toward the 12 hours.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the measurement rule 4.2.1 rests on. Where the period starts within the non-straight-through process is ambiguity A12.
clauses.operative_weight: The cooling-off clock may start before activation completes.

clauses.text: the responsible FI must provide notification alerts on a real-time basis to the account holder of a protected account, when (i) his digital security token is activated
clauses.assertion: When a digital security token was activated, a real-time alert was sent to the account holder.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on the activation event. `real-time` is undefined in both instruments (ambiguity A2); the fact records the FI's assessment that the alert was real-time, which is why the requirement is a held judgment rather than a timestamp comparison.

clauses.text: (ii) there is a login to a protected account issued by a relevant payment service provider on a new device
clauses.assertion: For a PSP-issued account, when a login occurred on a new device, a real-time alert was sent.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only for a PSP-issued account and only on a new-device login. For a bank-issued account the limb never arises.

note.value: not_applicable for a bank-issued account, or a PSP-issued account with no new-device login.

clauses.text: (iii) any high-risk activities are performed on a protected account
clauses.assertion: When a high-risk activity was performed, a real-time alert was sent.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on a high-risk activity as the SRF defines it (closed list).

clauses.text: The responsible FI provides notification alerts on a real-time basis, when a digital security token is activated or when there is a login ... on a new device, and for the conduct of high-risk activities
clauses.assertion: The 4.2.2 duty is discharged when each of its three limbs is satisfied or never arose.
clauses.disposition_basis: Composes the three limbs into the one duty Section 6 counts. A limb that never arose composes as holding (the limb is conditional by its words); whether a duty ALL of whose limbs never arose counts as complied with is A3, and the composition keeps `not_applicable` distinct from `satisfied` for that reason.

note.value: breached if any limb was; not_applicable only if all three never arose; satisfied needs every limb satisfied or never arisen; else undetermined.

clauses.source_locator: EUPG 3.1, p.8; SRF footnote 6, p.6, and footnote 17, p.13
clauses.text: The duties of the account holders in this Section 3 will apply to all the account holders that the responsible FI has been instructed to send transaction notifications to.
clauses.assertion: The account holder instructed the FI to send transaction notifications and provided the contact information for them.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded instruction. 4.2.3 arises only for an account holder the FI `has been instructed to send transaction notification alerts to`; an account holder who declined notifications has no 4.2.3 duty owed to them (ambiguity A20).

clauses.source_locator: EUPG 2.1 `transaction notification threshold` limb (a), p.5; SRF footnote 7, p.6
clauses.text: (a) the threshold for transaction alerts set by the account holder
clauses.assertion: Where the account holder set a threshold, the seemingly authorised transaction was above it.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where the holder set a threshold. The comparison of the amount against the threshold is mechanical in nature and the register has no ordered amount comparison (F-05), so it is taken as the FI's recorded assessment.

clauses.source_locator: EUPG 2.1 `transaction notification threshold` limb (b), p.5; SRF footnote 7, p.6
clauses.text: (b) if the account holder did not set any threshold for transaction alerts, the default industry-baseline transaction notification threshold
clauses.assertion: Where the holder set no threshold, the transaction was above the default industry-baseline threshold.
clauses.disposition_basis: Neither instrument states the baseline's value or who sets it. The term is ungrounded: the clause is undetermined until an institution supplies the baseline, and a determination made with a supplied baseline is marked as resting on it.

clauses.source_locator: SRF footnote 7, p.6; EUPG 2.1 `transaction notification threshold`, p.5
clauses.text: In line with the default industry-baseline transaction notification threshold or threshold for transaction alerts set by the account holder.
clauses.assertion: The transaction was one 4.2.3 requires an alert for: above whichever threshold applies.
clauses.disposition_basis: Selects limb (a) or (b) by whether the holder set a threshold, and reads that limb's result. Reads no fact of its own.

note.value: Selects the limb by whether the holder set a threshold. The _on_supplied_meaning tokens are carried, not laundered (F-08: the attribution stops at 4.2.3).

clauses.source_locator: SRF 4.2.3, p.6, with footnotes 6 and 7; EUPG 4.10, p.17-18
clauses.text: the responsible FI must provide transaction notification alerts to each account holder of a protected account that the responsible FI has been instructed to send transaction notification alerts to, in respect of all outgoing payment transactions made from the account holder's protected account
clauses.assertion: Where the account holder had instructed notifications and the transaction was above the applicable threshold, a real-time outgoing transaction alert was sent.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on two preconditions (instruction, threshold) and requires a real-time alert, which is the FI's recorded assessment (A2). The content criteria of EUPG 4.10(a)-(d) are not assessed by SRF 4.2.3, which names only provision on a real-time basis (ambiguity A21).

note.value: not_applicable: the holder did not instruct notifications, or the transaction was below the applicable threshold (A20). Whether the threshold rested on a supplied meaning is visible on srf/4.2.3/above-threshold, not here (F-08).

clauses.text: the responsible FI must provide account holders of protected accounts with a reporting channel that is available at all times for the purposes of prompt reporting and blocking of further seemingly authorised transactions
clauses.assertion: A reporting channel available at all times was provided.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded boolean about the channel's availability. Whether it was available at the moment of THIS claim, as opposed to in general, is ambiguity A22.

clauses.text: The reporting channel must include a self-service feature to promptly block further mobile and online access to the account holder's protected account.
clauses.assertion: The channel included a self-service feature that blocks further mobile and online access.
clauses.disposition_basis: Two recorded booleans, both required. `promptly` is undefined (A2's class) and is not tested.

clauses.text: The responsible FI provides a reporting channel and self-service feature for the account holder to promptly block further access to the protected account
clauses.assertion: The 4.2.4 duty is discharged when both the channel and the self-service feature were provided.
clauses.disposition_basis: Composes the two halves into the one duty Section 6 counts. This duty has no precondition, so it is never `not_applicable`.

note.value: No precondition: this duty is never not_applicable.

clauses.source_locator: SRF 4.4, p.7; media release of 24 October 2024, para 3
clauses.text: Paragraph 4.2.5 will take effect 6 months from the date these Guidelines are effective.
clauses.assertion: 4.2.5 applies to a seemingly authorised transaction executed on or after 16 June 2025.
clauses.disposition_basis: Orders the transaction's execution instant against a date. The date is derived (16 December 2024 plus six months) and the instrument does not state it as a calendar date; the media release says `a 6-month transition period` (ambiguity A23: which instant of a multi-transaction scam is the one ordered).

note.value: in_force when the transaction executed on or after 16 June 2025 (Singapore time). missing_operand: no execution instant recorded.

clauses.text: A protected account is considered to be rapidly drained of a material sum if (a) the protected account has account balance of S$50,000 or more immediately prior to the seemingly authorised transaction and (b) more than 50% of such account balance is transferred out within the last 24 hours.
clauses.assertion: The account held S$50,000 or more immediately before the transaction and more than half of it left within 24 hours, excluding the listed recurring and intrabank flows.
clauses.disposition_basis: Mechanical in nature and unexpressible here: no ordered comparison over amounts, no fraction, no hours unit (F-05). Taken as the FI's recorded assessment and routed to a person. `within the last 24 hours` is measured from an unstated instant (ambiguity A10).

note.value: Footnote 8, held rather than measured (F-05).

clauses.text: the responsible FI must have in place real-time fraud surveillance directed at detecting seemingly authorised transactions to a scammer(s)
clauses.assertion: Real-time fraud surveillance directed at seemingly authorised transactions was in place.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded boolean. Applies only from the commencement date, which srf/4.2.5/duty gates.

clauses.text: In a scenario where a protected account is rapidly drained of a material sum to a scammer, the responsible FI must: (a) Block the online banking payment transaction that would result in the crossing of the threshold ... until it is able to obtain further verification from the account holder; or (b) Send notification to the account holder, and block or hold for at least 24 hours
clauses.assertion: Where the account was rapidly drained of a material sum, the FI either blocked the crossing transaction and all subsequent ones to the scammer until verified, or notified the holder and held them for at least 24 hours.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on the footnote 8 condition, which is a held judgment; a judgment of `not_assessed` leaves the precondition unresolved and the clause undetermined rather than not applicable. The response is recorded as one of two named alternatives or `none`. The 24-hour minimum of (b) is not measured (F-05).

note.value: not_applicable: the account was not rapidly drained of a material sum. undetermined: nobody assessed whether it was.

clauses.text: The responsible FI puts in place real-time fraud surveillance directed at detecting unauthorised transactions in a phishing scam
clauses.assertion: From 16 June 2025, the 4.2.5 duty is discharged when surveillance was in place and, where the account was rapidly drained, the required response was made.
clauses.disposition_basis: Gates the two halves on the commencement clause. Before commencement the duty never arose (`not_applicable`); an unknown execution date leaves it undetermined.

note.value: not_applicable before 16 June 2025 (4.4). From commencement: surveillance in place is unconditional and the response is required only on a rapid drain.

clauses.text: Where relevant, paragraph 4.2 of these Guidelines applies during a scheduled system downtime. The responsible FI is to ensure continued delivery of key services and alternatives, where applicable.
clauses.assertion: Scheduled downtime does not suspend the 4.2 duties.
clauses.disposition_basis: Directs continued delivery `where relevant` and `where applicable`, neither of which the text defines (ambiguity A17). No fact of a claim makes it true or false; the 4.2 clauses are evaluated the same way whether or not downtime was scheduled.

clauses.text: the responsible FI has complied with all of its duties set out in paragraph 4.2 of these Guidelines
clauses.assertion: Each of the five 4.2 duties was complied with.
clauses.disposition_basis: A conjunction over the five duty results. A duty that never arose (`not_applicable`) is composed under ambiguity A3: with the resolution `counts_as_complied` it holds; with `not_a_compliance_finding` the conjunction is undetermined; unresolved, undetermined. NO DEFAULT: an absent resolution blocks the tier rather than reading the duty as discharged.

note.value: satisfied only on five affirmative results; a never-arisen duty composes under A3's supplied resolution and blocks the tier unresolved.

clauses.text: any non-compliance by the responsible FI with any duty set out in paragraph 4.2
clauses.assertion: At least one of the five 4.2 duties was breached.
clauses.disposition_basis: A disjunction over breach flags: one established breach decides it even if another duty is undetermined; no breach and one undetermined leaves it undetermined; five affirmative non-breach findings make it false.

note.value: true on one established breach whatever the others; false only on five affirmative non-breach results.

clauses.text: if the loss arises from any non-compliance by the responsible FI
clauses.assertion: The loss arose from the FI's non-compliance.
clauses.disposition_basis: Causation is assessed, never inferred from the breach. Whether 6.2 requires it at all, given 6.4(a)'s wording, is ambiguity A4; the register takes the words `arises from` as a condition and registers the reading that would drop it.

clauses.text: The responsible FI is expected to bear any loss arising from a seemingly authorised transaction if the loss arises from any non-compliance by the responsible FI with any duty set out in paragraph 4.2 of these Guidelines.
clauses.assertion: The FI bears the loss under 6.2 when a 4.2 duty was breached and the loss arose from that breach.
clauses.disposition_basis: A decision table over the breach disjunction and the causation judgment. Every combination is a row; a missing row throws.

rows.note: A 4.2 duty was breached and the loss arose from it.
A breach the loss did not arise from. Under A4's other reading this row would be fi_bears; the register encodes the words.
No breach; a causation finding has nothing to attach to.
Decided on five affirmative findings; the unassessed causation could not change it.
rows.$decided_on_absence: Five affirmative non-breach findings make causation moot: 6.2 attaches liability to non-compliance, and there is none to arise from.

clauses.source_locator: EUPG 5.5(a), p.26; SRF 6.3 and footnote 12, p.9
clauses.text: fraud or negligence by the responsible FI, its employee, its agent or any outsourcing service provider contracted by the responsible FI
clauses.assertion: The FI, an employee, agent or outsourcing provider was fraudulent or negligent.
clauses.disposition_basis: Negligence is assessed. Taken as an input.

clauses.source_locator: EUPG 5.5(b), p.26; SRF 6.3 and footnote 12, p.9
clauses.text: non-compliance by the responsible FI or its employee with any requirement imposed by the Authority on the responsible FI in respect of its provision of any financial service
clauses.assertion: The FI or an employee failed to comply with a requirement MAS imposed.
clauses.disposition_basis: `any requirement imposed by the Authority` is an open class the register cannot enumerate (ambiguity A16). Taken as an input.

clauses.source_locator: EUPG 5.5(c), p.26; SRF 6.3 and footnote 12, p.9
clauses.text: (c) non-compliance by the responsible FI with any duty set out in Section 4.
clauses.assertion: The SRF's footnote 12 incorporates 5.5(a) and (b) and NOT (c). A breach of an EUPG Section 4 duty outside SRF 4.2 does not shift loss under the SRF.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the boundary of 6.3. Tests nothing; the SRF's selective incorporation is ambiguity A24 (whether the omission of (c) was deliberate).

clauses.text: if the loss arises from any action or omission by the responsible FI as defined in paragraphs 5.5(a) and 5.5(b) of the EUPG
clauses.assertion: The loss arose from the fraud, negligence or MAS-requirement non-compliance found.
clauses.disposition_basis: Causation, assessed.

clauses.text: Notwithstanding paragraph 6.2 of these Guidelines, the responsible FI will be responsible for losses arising from a seemingly authorised transaction if the loss arises from any action or omission by the responsible FI as defined in paragraphs 5.5(a) and 5.5(b) of the EUPG
clauses.assertion: The FI is responsible under 6.3 when 5.5(a) or 5.5(b) is affirmed and the loss arose from it, whatever 6.2 says.
clauses.disposition_basis: A conjunction of (a disjunction over the two judgments) and the causation judgment. Reads no fact of its own.

note.value: satisfied: 5.5(a) or (b) affirmed AND the loss arose from it. not_satisfied on an affirmative denial of both, or of causation.

clauses.text: 6.5 For avoidance of doubt, where the responsible FI is expected to bear the loss under paragraph 6.2 of these Guidelines, the responsible FI will do so notwithstanding that the responsible Telco may have also failed to comply
clauses.assertion: The FI tier closes with `fi_bears` if either 6.2 or 6.3 attaches the loss to the FI; `fi_not_liable` only when both affirmatively do not; otherwise undetermined.
clauses.disposition_basis: A decision table over 6.2 and 6.3. `fi_not_liable` requires two affirmative findings; an undetermined on either side with no `fi_bears` on the other blocks the waterfall here.

rows.note: 6.2 decided it; 6.3 could not change it.
rows.$decided_on_absence: 6.2 alone attaches the loss to the FI; 6.3 is `notwithstanding 6.2` and can only add, never subtract.

rows.note: 6.3 decided it; 6.2 could not change it.
rows.$decided_on_absence: 6.3 alone attaches the loss to the FI; the unresolved 6.2 question could only reach the same answer.

clauses.text: the responsible FI next assesses if the seemingly authorised transaction resulted from a scammer impersonating an entity and contacting the account holder using SMS ("perpetrated through SMS")
clauses.assertion: The contact platform was SMS as the SRF defines it.
clauses.disposition_basis: Equality of the recorded contact platform with `sms`. The Telco tier arises only on this result.

note.value: The Telco tier arises only on `sms`. An OTT message is not_sms (2.1 `SMS`).

clauses.text: Responsible Telcos' duties are a specific subset of IMDA's directions to Telcos under section 31 of the Telecommunications Act 1999 ("IMDA's Directions"). For the avoidance of doubt, IMDA's Directions will prevail if there is any inconsistency
clauses.assertion: The 5.2 duties are read subject to IMDA's Directions, which are not retrieved.
clauses.disposition_basis: Directs which instrument prevails. IMDA's Directions are outside the retrieved sources (SOURCES.md); the register evaluates the SRF's wording of the three duties and cannot see an inconsistency (F-06).

clauses.text: The responsible Telco must deliver Sender ID SMS to subscribers only if it is received from authorised aggregators
clauses.assertion: Where the phishing SMS was a Sender ID SMS, it was received from an aggregator on the SGNIC list of authorised aggregators.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only for a Sender ID SMS and only in the Telco tier. Footnote 9 grounds `authorised aggregator` to the SGNIC list, which the register takes as a supplied register of names (ambiguity A7: membership at delivery time or at assessment time).

note.value: not_applicable: not perpetrated through SMS, or the SMS carried a telephone number rather than a Sender ID.

clauses.text: The responsible Telco must block Sender ID SMS which are received from sources other than authorised aggregators.
clauses.assertion: Where the phishing SMS was a Sender ID SMS from a source other than an authorised aggregator, it was blocked.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only for a Sender ID SMS from an unauthorised source. In a claim about an SMS the subscriber received the requirement is breached by construction; 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 describe one rule from two sides and a single unauthorised delivery breaches both (ambiguity A25: one duty or two for the purpose of `any duty`).

note.value: Arises only for a Sender ID SMS from an unauthorised source; breached when it was delivered. One unauthorised delivery breaches 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 together (A25).

clauses.text: The responsible Telco must implement an anti-scam filter for all SMS that pass through the responsible Telcos' network ... applies regardless of whether the SMS originates locally or from overseas
clauses.assertion: An anti-scam filter over all SMS was implemented.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded boolean, in the Telco tier only.

clauses.text: to determine if it contains any URL that matches that of a known malicious URL in a designated database
clauses.assertion: The database the filter matches against is the designated one.
clauses.disposition_basis: The text names no database and no designating authority; footnote 10 is a warning to the public. The term is ungrounded: undetermined until an institution supplies which database(s) are designated, and a determination made with a supplied meaning is marked as resting on it.

clauses.text: to block SMS containing malicious URLs in designated database
clauses.assertion: Where the phishing SMS's URL was in the designated database at delivery, the SMS was blocked.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where the URL was listed at delivery, which is a held judgment about the database's state at an instant. Whether 5.2.3 is breached by a filter that exists but let a listed URL through is ambiguity A5; this clause carries the reading that it is.

note.value: A5's second reading, as its own record. not_applicable: the URL was not listed at delivery (A6).

clauses.text: Responsible Telco implements an anti-scam filter over SMS to block SMS containing malicious URLs in designated database
clauses.assertion: The 5.2.3 duty is discharged on the reading the institution resolves A5 to: filter in place over the designated database, or that plus the specific SMS blocked.
clauses.disposition_basis: Guarded on A5. Unresolved, the duty is undetermined and the Telco tier cannot close. Reads no fact of its own.

note.value: Guarded on A5; unresolved, undetermined. `designated` on a supplied meaning composes as designated (the attribution is on srf/5.2.3/designated-database; F-08).

clauses.text: the loss arises from the responsible Telco's non-compliance with any duty set out in paragraph 5.2
clauses.assertion: At least one 5.2 duty was breached.
clauses.disposition_basis: A disjunction over breach flags, as for the FI. Outside the Telco tier every input is `not_applicable` and the disjunction is false, which the tier clause never reads because it gates on 7.7 first.

note.value: Outside the Telco tier every input is not_applicable and this is false; srf/6.4/telco-bears gates on 7.7 before reading it.

clauses.text: the loss arises from the responsible Telco's non-compliance
clauses.assertion: The loss arose from the Telco's non-compliance.
clauses.disposition_basis: Causation, assessed (A4's class).

clauses.text: In cases where the responsible Telco's subscriber is not the same as the account holder, the responsible Telco is expected to bear the loss under paragraph 6.4 of these Guidelines if: (a) the subscriber's mobile number is designated to receive SMS notifications pertaining to the protected account; and (b) the subscriber's mobile number which received the phishing SMS led to the seemingly authorised transaction
clauses.assertion: Where the subscriber is not the account holder, both (a) and (b) hold.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only when subscriber and account holder differ. `breached` here means the Telco does not bear under 6.6, not that anyone breached a duty; the token is the primitive's and the reading is at the composition. Which Telco is responsible when the subscriber's operator differs from the holder's is ambiguity A9.

note.value: not_applicable: the subscriber is the account holder. breached: the subscriber differs and (a) or (b) fails, so the Telco does not bear under 6.6.

clauses.text: The responsible Telco is expected to bear losses arising from a seemingly authorised transaction perpetrated through SMS if: (a) the responsible FI has complied with all of its duties set out in paragraph 4.2 of these Guidelines; and (b) the loss arises from the responsible Telco's non-compliance with any duty set out in paragraph 5.2
clauses.assertion: The Telco tier closes `telco_bears` only on: perpetrated through SMS, the FI complied with all 4.2 duties, a 5.2 duty was breached, the loss arose from it, and (where the subscriber differs) 6.6 holds. `not_applicable` when the scam was not perpetrated through SMS. An undetermined 5.2 duty blocks the tier before causation or 6.6 is read.
clauses.disposition_basis: Gates on 7.7, then decides in order: 6.4(a) affirmatively failing closes the tier not liable (6.5); an undetermined duty question blocks it; five affirmative non-breach findings close it not liable; only then are causation and 6.6 read, an affirmative denial closing it not liable and affirmative findings closing it telco_bears. Reads no fact of its own.

note.value: not_applicable: not perpetrated through SMS. telco_not_liable when the FI did not comply with all of 4.2 (6.5), or on five affirmative non-breach findings, or on an affirmative denial of causation or of 6.6 AFTER a breach is established. An undetermined 5.2 duty blocks the tier before causation is read. telco_bears on affirmative findings only.

clauses.text: where the responsible FI is expected to bear the loss under paragraph 6.2 of these Guidelines, the responsible FI will do so notwithstanding that the responsible Telco may have also failed to comply
clauses.assertion: The FI tier is evaluated first and `fi_bears` closes the waterfall whatever the Telco tier finds.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the ordering that srf/6.7/outcome's table encodes. Tests nothing of its own.
clauses.operative_weight: fi_bears dominates every Telco-tier result, including undetermined.

clauses.text: Where the responsible FI is not expected to bear the loss under paragraph 6.2 of these Guidelines, and the responsible Telco is not expected to bear the loss under paragraph 6.4 of these Guidelines, the account holder of a protected account should bear any loss arising from a seemingly authorised transaction.
clauses.assertion: The account holder bears the loss only on two affirmative findings: the FI tier closed `fi_not_liable` and the Telco tier closed `telco_not_liable` or never arose. An out-of-scope claim leaves the SRF (`out_of_scope`, 7.6). Undetermined scope or an undetermined tier is undetermined here.
clauses.disposition_basis: Gated on scope, then a decision table over the two tiers. The only path to `account_holder_bears` is through affirmative non-liability findings on both prior tiers; no row defaults to it.

rows.note: Unreachable in a consistent run (telco_bears requires 6.4(a)), listed because a missing row is a defect.

rows.$decided_on_absence: 6.5: the FI bears notwithstanding whatever the Telco tier would find.

rows.note: 6.7 with 6.4 never arising (not perpetrated through SMS). The Telco tier's not_applicable is an affirmative finding that 7.7 answered `not_sms`, never an absent fact.
Inconsistent (telco_bears needs the FI tier closed); undetermined rather than trusted.
Out of scope whatever the tiers computed: the tiers are evaluated for the record and allocate nothing under the SRF.
