clauses.source_locator: SRF footnote 11, p.8; EUPG footnote 19, p.23
clauses.text: losses arising from unauthorised transactions exclude any loss of business or profit, special, punitive, indirect or consequential loss and any other losses
clauses.assertion: The loss the waterfall allocates is the transaction amount, not consequential loss.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the meaning of `loss` in 7.13 and 7.14.
clauses.operative_weight: `total loss` in 7.13 and 7.14 is the sum of the seemingly authorised transactions.

clauses.text: Notwithstanding paragraph 6.7 of these Guidelines where the account holder is deemed responsible, the account holder may seek alternative channels for redress as explained in Section 7.
clauses.assertion: An account_holder_bears outcome is not final against the account holder.
clauses.disposition_basis: Permits an act. No fact makes it true or false.

clauses.text: Where the protected account is a joint account, the responsibility for losses set out in this Section apply jointly to each account holder in a joint account.
clauses.assertion: An account_holder_bears outcome binds every joint holder.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the meaning of `account holder` in 6.7 for a joint account. The register records `account.joint` and nothing reads it: the outcome token does not change per holder.
clauses.operative_weight: One outcome for the account, binding all holders.

clauses.text: account users should only refer to official sources for information on the website addresses and phone numbers of their responsible FIs
clauses.assertion: The account user used official sources for the FI's contact details.
clauses.disposition_basis: Whether a source was `official` is assessed from the account of the incident. NOT READ BY THE WATERFALL: Section 6 allocates loss on FI and Telco duties only; an account user's breach of Section 3 changes nothing in 6.7 (ambiguity A19).

note.value: Not read by Section 6 (A19).

clauses.text: account users should not click on links provided in SMS or emails, unless these are informational links that the account user is expecting to receive from the responsible FI
clauses.assertion: The account user did not click an unexpected link.
clauses.disposition_basis: Expectation is assessed. Not read by the waterfall (A19).

note.value: affirmed means the user clicked an unexpected link. Not read by Section 6 (A19).

clauses.text: The account holder of a protected account should activate the kill switch provided by the responsible FI ... as soon as practicable, after he is notified of any unauthorised transactions and has reason to believe that the account has been compromised, or if he is unable to contact the responsible FI.
clauses.assertion: The account holder activated the kill switch as soon as practicable after notice.
clauses.disposition_basis: `as soon as practicable` and `reason to believe` are assessed. Not read by the waterfall (A19).

note.value: Not read by Section 6 (A19).

clauses.text: The account holder of a protected account is liable for actual loss arising from an unauthorised transaction where any account user's recklessness was the primary cause of the loss.
clauses.assertion: An account user's recklessness was the primary cause of the loss.
clauses.disposition_basis: Assessed. NOT read by the SRF waterfall: Section 6 allocates loss without a recklessness test, and 6.7 reaches the account holder only through the FI's and Telco's compliance (A19). Encoded so the divergence between the two instruments' consumer tiers is a record, not a remark.

note.value: EUPG liability, not SRF allocation. Not read by Section 6 (A19).

clauses.text: the account holder, responsible FI and responsible Telco (where applicable) should adhere to the following four-stage workflow: (a) Claim Stage ... (b) Investigation Stage ... (c) Outcome Stage ... (d) Recourse Stage
clauses.assertion: The workflow has four stages in this order.
clauses.disposition_basis: Directs a sequence. The stages' own requirements are the 7.2 to 7.14 clauses.

clauses.text: A responsible FI should explain the operational workflow to the account holder ... at the time the account holder reports the seemingly authorised transaction to the responsible FI, and inform the account holder of the timeline for investigation
clauses.assertion: At the time of the report, the FI explained the workflow and the investigation timeline.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded boolean.

clauses.text: The account holder should report any unauthorised activity to the responsible FI as soon as practicable, and no later than 30 calendar days from when the responsible FI sends the notification alerts
clauses.assertion: The report reached the FI within 30 calendar days of the FI sending the first alert.
clauses.disposition_basis: An interval against a limit. The SRF counts from when the FI SENDS; EUPG 3.14 counts from RECEIPT (ambiguity A8a). The effect of a late report on the Section 6 outcome is not stated (ambiguity A8); nothing in the waterfall reads this clause.

note.value: The SRF clock: from the FI sending the first alert (A8a). No Section 6 consequence is encoded (A8).

clauses.text: Where the account holder is not able to report ... within the stipulated time period, the account holder should, if the responsible FI so requests, provide the responsible FI with reasons for the delayed report.
clauses.assertion: Where the report was late and the FI asked for reasons, reasons were given.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on two preconditions, one of which is the result of the 30-day clause.

note.value: not_applicable: the report was in time, or the FI did not ask.

clauses.text: The account holder must furnish a valid email address, and any other supporting information such as a police report and digital communication trail(s), within 3 calendar days from the date of notification of the seemingly authorised transaction to the responsible FI
clauses.assertion: A valid email address and the supporting information were furnished within 3 calendar days of the report.
clauses.disposition_basis: A presence test and an interval. `any other supporting information such as` is open; the register records the instant the holder's submission was made and the email flag, not the sufficiency of the submission.

note.value: no_email: no valid email address was furnished. Otherwise elapsed_within's tokens over the 3 days from the report.

clauses.text: The communication records should sufficiently demonstrate that: (a) the scammer posed as an impersonated entity; (b) there is an intent to obtain account credentials under false pretences; and (c) the scammer directed the account holder to a digital platform of the impersonated entity to enter his account credentials.
clauses.assertion: The records supplied demonstrate each of (a), (b) and (c).
clauses.disposition_basis: `sufficiently demonstrate` is assessed. Three held judgments composed by conjunction; a `not_assessed` on any leaves the clause undetermined. NOT read by the scope clauses: whether the scam WAS a seemingly authorised transaction (2.1) and whether the records DEMONSTRATE it (7.4) are different questions (ambiguity A26).

note.value: Not read by 7.1.1 (A26).

clauses.text: the name of the responsible Telco whose services the account holder had subscribed to and associated mobile phone number ... (a) the mobile number of the account user; and (b) the details and screenshot of the purported SMS
clauses.assertion: Where the scam was perpetrated through SMS, the Telco's name, the mobile number and the SMS details were supplied.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only in an SMS case.

clauses.text: Upon enquiry by an account holder, the responsible FI is expected to provide the account holder with relevant information that the responsible FI has of all the seemingly authorised transactions ... including transaction dates, transaction timestamps and parties to the transaction.
clauses.assertion: Where the account holder enquired, the FI provided the transaction information.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on an enquiry.

clauses.text: Where the responsible FI has assessed that a claim brought by an account holder does not involve a seemingly authorised transaction, the responsible FI investigates the claim based on its existing investigation and claim resolution process ... The responsible FI should communicate its assessment and claim resolution process to the account holder in a timely and transparent manner.
clauses.assertion: Where the claim is not a relevant claim, the FI communicated its assessment and its claim resolution process.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only on a `not_relevant` scope result. `timely and transparent` is not tested.

note.value: not_applicable: a relevant claim, which Section 6 allocates.

clauses.text: If so, the responsible FI should inform the responsible Telco, for the responsible Telco to commence its investigation. The responsible FI should obtain from the account holder relevant information on the scam perpetrated through SMS before referring the claim
clauses.assertion: In an SMS case that is a relevant claim, the FI informed the responsible Telco.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on two clause results. Footnote 13 makes the Telco's involvement depend on a mutually agreed arrangement the register cannot see (ambiguity A27).

clauses.text: (a) Scam was perpetrated through SMS: The responsible FI and responsible Telco investigate concurrently whether each of them has fulfilled their duties under paragraphs 4.2 and 5.2, respectively. (b) Scam was not perpetrated through SMS: The responsible FI investigates whether it has fulfilled its duties under paragraph 4.2.
clauses.assertion: Investigation is concurrent, not sequential; the allocation in Section 6 is what is ordered.
clauses.disposition_basis: Directs who investigates. The register's emit order is the Section 6 allocation order, not an investigation order.

clauses.text: A responsible FI and a responsible Telco should have governance structures and investigations processes, involving representatives who are independent from business units, to assess and determine whether duties have been breached.
clauses.assertion: The FI's assessment involved representatives independent from business units.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded boolean about the process.

clauses.text: A responsible FI and a responsible Telco should have governance structures and investigations processes, involving representatives who are independent from business units
clauses.assertion: In an SMS case, the Telco's assessment involved representatives independent from business units.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only in an SMS case.

clauses.text: The responsible FI, and responsible Telco where applicable, should complete an investigation of any relevant claim within 21 business days for straightforward cases or 45 business days for complex cases.
clauses.assertion: The investigation was completed within 21 business days (straightforward) or 45 business days (complex) of the report.
clauses.disposition_basis: An interval against a limit selected by the recorded complexity classification. The classification is the FI's (the SRF gives one example); an unrecorded classification leaves the clause undetermined rather than defaulting to 21. Business days are counted as weekdays; Singapore public holidays are not excluded (ambiguity A28).

note.value: The limit is selected by the FI's recorded classification; unrecorded is undetermined, never 21. Weekdays only (A28).

clauses.text: All relevant logs or documentation to assess SRF claims and demonstrate compliance with the SRF duties are expected to be retained for a reasonable period of time.
clauses.assertion: Logs and documentation are retained.
clauses.disposition_basis: `a reasonable period` is not a limit the register can measure against; directs retention.

clauses.text: The responsible FI should within the stipulated periods in paragraph 7.9 provide each account holder ... a written reply of the investigation outcome and the assessment of the account holder's responsibility. The responsible FI should seek acknowledgement, which need not be an agreement
clauses.assertion: A written reply was given and acknowledgement sought.
clauses.disposition_basis: Two recorded booleans. Whether the reply was within the 7.9 period is the 7.9 clause's question, not repeated here.

clauses.text: the account holder may pursue further action through existing avenues of recourse as appropriate ... such as FIDReC ... or through writing to IMDA
clauses.assertion: Recourse is available; the SRF outcome is not final.
clauses.disposition_basis: Permits an act.

clauses.text: A longer implementation timeline will be provided for amendments to paragraphs 4.21, 6.4, 6.5, and Section 8 of these Guidelines, which will take effect on 16 June 2025.
clauses.assertion: EUPG 4.21 and Section 8 apply to a transaction executed on or after 16 June 2025.
clauses.disposition_basis: Orders the execution instant against a stated date. Same instant question as A23.

note.value: in_force when the transaction executed on or after 16 June 2025 (Singapore time).

clauses.source_locator: EUPG 8.1, p.35; SRF 7.12 with footnote 18, p.14
clauses.text: Where an account holder reports a suspected unauthorised transaction ("disputed transaction"), the responsible FI should withhold and/or waive the requirement for the account holder to settle the outstanding amount of the disputed transaction and the charges directly relating to the disputed transaction until the responsible FI completes its investigation
clauses.assertion: From 16 June 2025, charges relating to the disputed transaction were withheld or waived pending investigation.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded boolean, gated on the deferred commencement. SRF 7.12 applies Section 8 `where relevant`; 8.2 to 8.6 are not encoded (F-02).

note.value: not_applicable before 16 June 2025 (EUPG 1.5).

clauses.text: The responsible FI should credit the account holder's protected account with the total loss arising from any seemingly authorised transaction in accordance with the framework on assessment of responsibilities for losses set out in Section 6
clauses.assertion: Where the outcome is fi_bears, the FI credited the total loss.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on the waterfall outcome. The register does not compare the credited amount to the loss (F-05); the fact is the FI's recorded flag.

note.value: Arises only on an fi_bears outcome.

clauses.text: The responsible Telco should credit the account holder with the total loss (as verified by the responsible FI) ... based on a mutually agreed payment modality with the account holder.
clauses.assertion: Where the outcome is telco_bears, the Telco credited the total loss.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on the waterfall outcome. `mutually agreed payment modality` is not tested.

note.value: Arises only on a telco_bears outcome.

clauses.text: The account holder of a protected account should report any unauthorised activity to the responsible FI as soon as practicable, and no later than 30 calendar days after receipt of any notification alert for any unauthorised activity
clauses.assertion: The report was made within 30 calendar days of the holder receiving the first alert.
clauses.disposition_basis: The same 30 days as SRF 7.3, measured from receipt rather than sending (A8a). Encoded separately so the two clocks are two records.

note.value: The EUPG clock: from receipt (A8a).

clauses.text: The account holder of a protected account should within a reasonable time provide the responsible FI with any of the following information as requested by the responsible FI
clauses.assertion: Where the FI requested 3.18 information, the holder provided it within a reasonable time.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on a request. `reasonable time` is assessed, so the requirement is a held judgment.

clauses.text: The account holder should also furnish the police report to the responsible FI within 3 calendar days of the responsible FI's request to do so
clauses.assertion: Where the FI requested a police report, it was furnished within 3 calendar days.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises on a request; the requirement is an interval. A report not yet furnished with the 3 days still running is `outstanding`, which is neither breach nor satisfaction.

note.value: outstanding: requested, not yet furnished, 3 days still running. out_of_order (furnished before the request) satisfies.

clauses.text: Notwithstanding paragraph 4.10, a responsible FI can elect to comply with an account holder's transaction notification alert preferences.
clauses.assertion: An account holder's instruction to receive fewer notifications narrows 4.10, and so 4.2.3.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the meaning of `has been instructed` in 4.2.3 (A20).
clauses.operative_weight: A transaction the holder instructed the FI not to notify is outside 4.2.3.

clauses.text: A responsible FI should provide a kill switch for an account holder to promptly block further mobile and online access to his protected account. This includes disallowing mobile and online payment transfers to third parties who are not authorised billers. The kill switch should be made available in a prominent manner via the mobile application ... the automated teller machines ... or the reporting channel
clauses.assertion: The kill switch disallowed transfers to non-billers, terminated existing sessions and was available prominently through a listed channel.
clauses.disposition_basis: Three recorded booleans. NOT read by SRF 4.2.4, which names only the self-service feature and the block (ambiguity A21's class); this is an EUPG duty the SRF does not assess.

note.value: Not read by SRF 4.2.4 (A21).

clauses.text: (b) Any person who makes a report through the reporting channel should receive a written acknowledgement of his report through SMS, email, or in-app notification. (c) The responsible FI should not charge a fee
clauses.assertion: The report was acknowledged in writing and no fee was charged.
clauses.disposition_basis: Two recorded booleans. Not read by SRF 4.2.4.

note.value: Not read by SRF 4.2.4 (A21).

clauses.text: A responsible FI should have in place capabilities to detect and block suspected unauthorised transactions at all times ... A responsible FI should review the effectiveness of its detection parameters for suspected unauthorised transactions on an annual basis, or as and when there are material triggers.
clauses.assertion: From 16 June 2025, detection-and-blocking capability was in place at all times and its parameters were reviewed annually.
clauses.disposition_basis: Two recorded booleans gated on the deferred commencement. SRF 4.2.5 is `[From paragraph 4.21]` but states a narrower, threshold-triggered duty; the EUPG's general capability duty is not what Section 6 assesses (A21's class).

note.value: Not read by SRF 4.2.5 (A21).
